cervinia-zermatt.notes:
Area skeletons — 41 polygons (A + B' + B), 365 portals (96 mid-boundary gateways), 0 stranded, 9 synthesised spines, 1 of them spined gateway-to-gateway because the polygon is too squat to be a run in its own right (a corridor between its neighbours), 10 spine stitches (1 polygons still split).
dark blue = existing centreline (reused spine) · light blue = synthesised spine (case B: no centreline exists, so one is invented down the middle) · turquoise = stitch joining two spine pieces that were otherwise separate components · pink = synthesised fan-out arm · purple = arm to a local hub (an interior lobe with no centreline of its own) · teal = polygon with no centreline through it at all, so arms link portal-to-portal · grey = polygon rim (for reference) · orange dot = portal · green dot = gateway: either the mid-point of a genuinely shared rim (one new node serving both polygons) or an existing node where two polygons touch at a single point · red dot = stranded portal.
